You are fixing how failures are scoped in ONE Python file. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. scripts/identity_proposals.py   (edit it)
  2. fix-summary.md                  (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check.

## What was measured live this morning

The generator was run twice against the real inbox with real credentials. The first run produced 5 email proposals. The second, from identical code, produced 0 and reported the channel unreadable. A per-name probe found why:

    record #0:  HTTP 200  matches=1  with_address=1
    record #1:  HTTP 200  matches=1  with_address=1
    record #4:  HTTP 200  matches=1  with_address=1
    record #11: HTTP 200  matches=1  with_address=1
    record #12: HTTP 429  You have reached your secondly limit.
    record #13: HTTP 429  You have reached your secondly limit.

Six searches fired back to back; HubSpot rate-limits per second and refuses the last two. In build_proposals, ONE try wraps the ENTIRE per-source loop, so that single 429 discarded the four proposals already collected and marked the whole channel unreachable. The lane was flaky by construction, not by circumstance, and it failed in the direction that loses good work.

## Three changes

### 1. Scope the failure to the candidate, not the source

Move the error handling inside the per-candidate loop. A lookup that raises produces an unresolved entry for THAT person and nothing else; every other candidate on the same source keeps its result. Somebody else's rate limit is not a reason to lose this person's answer.

A source is only reached=False when the source itself was unusable — no client could be built. If the client existed and lookups ran, coverage is reached=True even when some individual lookups failed; the per-candidate unresolved entries carry those failures. Do not invent a third coverage state.

### 2. Say what the failure was

An unresolved entry for a failed lookup must carry the HTTP status when there is one, e.g. "lookup failed: HTTP 429". A status number is not sensitive and it is the difference between 'retry in a moment' and 'this will never work'. Keep scrubbing the rest: never let a URL, query string, token or account identifier into the text — build the message from the status and the exception class only.

urllib raises urllib.error.HTTPError, which carries `.code`. Use it when present; fall back to the exception class name otherwise.

### 3. Stop causing the rate limit

Pace the requests so a normal run does not trip a per-second limit: a small delay between lookups on the same source is enough, and on a 429 specifically, wait briefly and retry that one lookup ONCE before giving up on it. Keep it simple and bounded — no exponential backoff library, no unbounded retry loop, no threading. Six lookups must comfortably complete.

## What must NOT change

  * exactly one plausible match proposes; two or more propose nobody and record the ambiguity; zero records "no match";
  * a candidate who already has a usable email is never looked up anywhere;
  * a cold candidate's name never reaches HubSpot and a warm one's never reaches Unipile;
  * every proposal carries evidence and a confidence derived from what corroborated it;
  * nothing is applied and nothing is marked confirmed;
  * names are carried, intake note text is not;
  * the artifact is written atomically at 0600;
  * the Unipile client keeps POSTing the classic people search and normalising first_name/last_name.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u20_identity_proposals_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

It now drives a client that answers the first lookup and then refuses with a 429, and requires the first answer to survive and the failure to name its status. It currently fails with one_failure_discarded_the_rest and failure_status_hidden.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' say what happens now if a source rate-limits every single lookup. Under 400 words.
tasks.verified: Drives the generator with a client that answers one lookup and then rate-limits, and requires the successful proposal to survive and the failed lookup's unresolved entry to carry its HTTP status. Every earlier assertion still executes — single-match proposes, ambiguous proposes nobody, reachable records are never looked up, cold names never reach HubSpot, raw Unipile shapes are normalised, no note text, no auto-apply, and the real command line with no credentials writes a private explained empty queue.
